text: At the very start, God created the heavens and the earth.
Then God said, “Let there be light,” and just like that, light showed up.
God checked out everything he made, and honestly, it was all pretty awesome. Then evening came, morning followed, and just like that, day six wrapped up.
So after Moses passed away, the Lord hit up Joshua, Moses’ right-hand guy, and said,
“Moses is gone; it’s time for you to step up, cross this Jordan with all your crew, and claim the land I’m giving to the Israelites.”
“Every spot your feet touch is yours, just like I promised Moses.”
“From the wilds and Lebanon all the way to the Euphrates River, and all the Hittite territory to the big sea at sunset, that’s your turf.”
“No one will be able to take you down for as long as you live. I was with Moses, and I’ll be with you too. I’ve got your back, no matter what.”
“So be strong and brave; you’re gonna share this land as an inheritance with the people, just like I promised their ancestors.”
“Just stay strong and super courageous. Follow all the laws Moses gave you. Don’t stray from them—keep focused so you can thrive wherever you go.”
“Keep this Book of the Law close; think about it day and night so you can live by everything in it. Then you’ll succeed, and things will go well for you.”
“Didn’t I tell you? Be strong and brave. Don’t be scared or discouraged, because the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”
Then Joshua rallied the leaders of the people, saying,
“Go through the camp and tell everyone to get ready. In three days, we’re crossing this Jordan to take over the land the Lord your God is giving us.”
Joshua also spoke to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, saying,
“Remember what Moses told you? The Lord your God has given you rest and this land.”
“Your families and livestock can chill in the land Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan, but you guys need to step up for your brothers—be ready to fight alongside them.”

“Once your brothers find rest like you have and claim the land the Lord your God is giving them, you can head back to your own territory and enjoy what Moses gave you on this side toward the sunrise.”
They replied to Joshua, “Whatever you say, we’re in. Wherever you send us, we’ll go.”
“Just like we listened to Moses in everything, we’ll listen to you too. Just make sure the Lord your God is with you like he was with Moses.”
“Anyone who rebels against what you say or ignores your commands will be dealt with seriously. Just stay strong and brave.”
After six days, Jesus grabbed Peter, James, and his brother John and took them up a chill mountain, just the four of them.
Then, out of nowhere, he totally transformed; his face was shining like the sun, and his clothes were super bright, like light.
And suddenly, Moses and Elijah showed up, just vibing and chatting with him.
Peter was like, “Yo, Jesus, this is awesome! Let’s set up three tents here—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
While he was still talking, a bright cloud rolled in and covered them. Then a voice from the cloud said, “This is my beloved Son; I’m stoked about him—listen to what he says.”
The disciples heard this and hit the ground in fear.
Jesus came over, touched them, and said, “Get up; don’t be scared.”
When they looked up, they only saw Jesus—no one else around.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus told them not to spill the tea about what they saw until he rises from the dead.
The disciples were curious and asked him, “Why do the scribes say Elijah has to come first?”
Jesus was like, “For real, Elijah’s gotta come first and fix everything up.”
“But here’s the tea: Elijah’s already been here, and they totally missed him. They did whatever they wanted to him. Same vibes for the Son of Man; he’s gonna go through it too.”
Then the disciples finally got it; he was talking about John the Baptist.
When they got back to the crowd, a dude came up, kneeling and saying,
“Lord, please help my son! He’s really struggling; he has these crazy fits where he falls into fire and water.
“I brought him to your disciples, but they couldn’t help him.”
Jesus replied, “Wow, you guys are lacking faith. How long do I have to deal with this? Bring him over here.”
Jesus told the evil spirit to bounce, and it left him. The kid was healed right then and there.
Later, the disciples pulled Jesus aside and asked, “Why couldn’t we kick it out?”

Jesus said, “It’s because you didn’t believe. For real, if you have faith even just a little bit, like a mustard seed, you could tell this mountain to move, and it would. Nothing would be impossible for you.”
“But honestly, some things only change with prayer and fasting.”
While they were chilling in Galilee, Jesus told them, “The Son of Man is gonna get betrayed by people.
“They’ll kill him, but on the third day, he’ll be back.” They were really feeling down about it.
When they got to Capernaum, some folks collecting taxes asked Peter, “Doesn’t your guy pay taxes?”
Peter was like, “Yeah.” But when he got home, Jesus was already on it, asking, “So, Simon, who do the kings of the earth collect taxes from—their kids or outsiders?”
Peter replied, “Outsiders.” Jesus said, “Exactly. So the kids are good.
“But just to keep the peace, go to the sea, throw in a hook, and catch the first fish you pull up. Open its mouth, and you’ll find a coin. Use that to pay for both of us.”
So the disciples rolled up to Jesus and were like, “Who’s the GOAT in the kingdom of heaven?”
Jesus called over a little kid and had him stand right there with them,
and said, “For real, unless you switch it up and become like these kids, you can’t even vibe in the kingdom of heaven.”
Whoever humbles themselves like this little one is actually the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And anyone who welcomes a kid like this in my name is welcoming me.
But if you mess with one of these little believers, it’d be better for you to have a huge stone tied around your neck and be tossed into the ocean.
Like, woe to the world for all the mess-ups! Offenses are gonna happen, but woe to the person causing them!
So if your hand or foot is tripping you up, just cut it off and toss it away. It’s better to enter life kinda broken than to have two hands or feet and end up in eternal fire.
And if your eye is causing issues, pluck it out and throw it away. Better to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and get tossed into hellfire.
Just know, don’t look down on any of these little ones; I’m telling you, their angels are always seeing my Father’s face in heaven.
The Son of Man came to save what was lost, you know?
So, like, what do you think? If a dude has a hundred sheep and one goes missing, wouldn’t he leave the ninety-nine to find the one that strayed?
And if he finds it, I’m telling you, he’s way happier about that one sheep than the ninety-nine that didn’t wander off.
For real though, it’s not the vibe for your Father in heaven to lose even one of these little ones.
And if your bro messes up with you, just go talk to him about it, just the two of you. If he listens, you’ve totally won him back.
But if he doesn’t listen, grab one or two friends with you so that everything’s legit with some witnesses.
If he still won’t hear them, then let the church know; but if he ignores the church too, treat him like someone who’s out of the crew.
For real, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed up there too.
Again, I’m saying to you, if two of you agree on anything down here and ask for it, my Father in heaven will make it happen.
Because where two or three are gathered in my name, I’m right there with them.
So Peter rolls up to Jesus and asks, “Yo, how many times should I forgive my bro when he messes up? Like, seven times?”
Jesus replies, “Nah, not just seven times. I’m talking seventy times seven. Keep it going.”
The kingdom of heaven is kinda like a king who decided to check in on his servants.
When he started counting, one servant was brought to him who owed a crazy amount—ten thousand talents.
But since the dude couldn’t pay up, the king ordered that he, his wife, and kids be sold off to settle the debt.
The servant fell down and begged, “Please, just give me some time and I’ll pay you back everything!”
The king felt for him, let him go, and wiped his debt clean.
“Not gonna lie, but that servant headed out, and found one of his fellow servants, who owed him one hundred denarii, and he grabbed him, and took him by the throat, ‘Pay me what you owe!’
“Lowkey, so his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I’m gonna repay you!’
Listen, he wouldn’t, but went and cast him into prison, until he should pay back that which was due, no cap.
When his coworkers saw what went down, they were super bummed and went to tell their boss everything that happened.
Then his lord called him in, and told him, ‘You shady servant! I forgave you guys that debt, because you begged me.
Real talk, shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’
Not gonna lie, his lord was heated, and delivered him to the tormentors, until he should pay all that was due to him.
Real talk, so my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don’t each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.”
So, after Jesus wrapped up his chat, he left Galilee and headed over to Judea, crossing the Jordan.
The kingdom of heaven is kinda like a dude who owns a vineyard and goes out early to hire some workers.
He made a deal with them for a penny a day and sent them to work in his vineyard.
Then, around mid-morning, he saw some folks just chilling in the marketplace, doing nothing.
He told them, “Hey, go work in my vineyard, and I’ll pay you what’s fair.” So they bounced.
He did the same thing around noon and again at three in the afternoon.
Then, right before closing time, he found more people standing around and asked, “Why are you guys just hanging out all day?”
They replied, “No one’s hired us.” He said, “Go work in the vineyard; I’ll pay you what’s right.”
When evening came, the vineyard owner told his manager, “Call the workers and pay them, starting with the last ones first.”
So those who were hired at the last hour got paid a penny each.
But when the first ones showed up, they thought they’d get more but ended up getting just a penny too.
When they got their pay, they started complaining to the boss of the house,
saying, “These last guys only worked one hour, and you made them equal to us who worked all day in the heat.”
But he replied to one of them, “Chill, friend, I didn’t do you wrong. Didn’t we agree on a penny?”
“Take what’s yours and bounce. I’m giving this last guy the same as you.”
“Is it not my call to do what I want with my own stuff? Is your vibe off just because I’m being good?”
“So the last will be first, and the first will be last; many are called, but few are chosen.”
As Jesus was heading to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside and said to them,
“Yo, we’re going up to Jerusalem; the Son of Man is gonna be betrayed to the chief priests and scribes, and they’re gonna condemn him to death,
“and hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, beat up, and crucify him. But on the third day, he’s rising again.”
Then the mom of Zebedee’s kids came to him with her sons, worshipping him and asking for something.
He asked her, “What do you want?” She replied, “Can my two sons sit next to you, one on your right and the other on your left in your kingdom?”
Jesus said, “You guys have no idea what you’re asking. Can you handle the cup I’m about to drink and the baptism I’m getting?” They said, “For sure, we can.”
Jesus told them, “You will drink from my cup and be baptized like I will be, but sitting on my right or left? That’s not mine to give. It’s for those my Father has prepared it for.”
When the other ten heard this, they were lowkey annoyed with the two brothers.
Jesus called everyone over and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles boss everyone around, and those who are great flex their authority.
“But it shouldn’t be like that with you. If you want to be great, be a servant instead;
“and if you want to be the top dog, be a servant too.
“Just like how the Son of Man didn’t come to be served but to serve and give his life as a ransom for many.”
As they were leaving Jericho, a huge crowd was following him.
And then there were two blind guys sitting by the road. When they heard Jesus was passing by, they shouted, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!”
The crowd was like, “Chill out, you guys,” but they just shouted louder, “Please have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!”
Jesus stopped and called them over, asking, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They replied, “Lord, we just want our eyes to be opened.”
Jesus felt for them and touched their eyes; instantly, they could see and started following him.
